references.text: The Letter to the Hebrews interprets 'rest' from Deuteronomy as a type of the spiritual rest that God's people are to enter through faith, and cites this concept directly.
Joshua reminds the people that the Lord will give them rest in the promised land, which is the fulfillment of the promise mentioned in Deuteronomy 12:9.
Describes how the Lord gave Israel rest from all their enemies, as a fulfillment of the promise of rest and inheritance.
Solomon praises the Lord for having given his people Israel rest, in accordance with all that he had promised.
God swears in his anger that they shall not enter into his rest, referring to the same rest promised in Deuteronomy.
Describes Zion as the Lord's resting place forever, his dwelling which he has chosen—linked to the concept of rest and inheritance.
